newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma puts off budget cuts bill.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma puts off budget cuts bill.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament decided on Wednesday to put off a debate on budget cuts proposed by the government until Friday.

Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais will present a bill on cutting or sequestering planned spending on Friday. The bill was originally due to have been presented on Wednesday, with debate and a vote following on Friday.
Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin as saying he hoped to reach a compromise with the communist-dominated chamber on budget cuts prompted by poor tax revenues.
Chernomyrdin had earlier indicated that the actual cuts may be less than the 20 percent envisaged in the government plan.
After a day of heated debates on the budget results for the first quarter, the Duma failed to adopt a final resolution denouncing the government's performance as unsatisfactory.

The debate on budget cuts will become the first test for Boris Yeltsin's commitment to carry out the new govenment programme he had approved earlier this week which is based on tough control of spending.
